PlayStation emerges victorious in a $2.6 billion lawsuit alleging a digital monopoly
The now-dismissed lawsuit accused PlayStation of setting "excessive and unfair prices" in the UK, but will not proceed any further.
Imran Khan
,
Contributing Editor
,
GameDeveloper.com
November 18, 2026
schedule
2 Min Read
Image via PlayStation
A $2.6 billion class action lawsuit brought in the United Kingdom against PlayStation has been dismissed by London's Competition Appeal Tribunal, clearing PlayStation of unfair practices that were alleged when the lawsuit was filed in 2023,
noted by VGC
.
The lawsuit, brought by UK consumer rights activist Alex Neil and representing the UK's 8.9 million PlayStation customers, argued that Sony's 30 percent cut on all digital purchases made on the PlayStation store while also determining prices on said store constitute an abuse of its dominant position and lead to excessive prices.
On the
website for the class action
, Neill and her lawyers argue that the current dynamic is rife for abuse and Sony is overcharging relative to the costs of these products.
"The business model of gaming has changed dramatically over recent years," the site reads. "The move from games sold as physical disks to games sold digitally has seen the introduction of in-game content, where players must now also pay to progress, unlock more features, or customize their experience with new characters or weapons. Games are now designed to incentivize players to spend as much money as possible (including children)."
Related:
Shigeru Miyamoto selected as inaugural Legend Award inductee at DICE Awards
The appeal tribunal did not agree with Neill's arguments, though perhaps not for enduring reasons. Part of the tribunal's reasoning is that PlayStation cannot maintain a monopoly over digital sales when physical sales are a consumer option, production of which
PlayStation will be abandoning in 2028
. But overall, the court was not swayed by the argument that PlayStation games were priced too high on the platform's digital store, so it is unlikely the removal of physical games as an option will change the tribunal's minds.
The lawsuit proceeding would have likely forced Sony to adjust its 30 percent fees for video game developers, significantly eroding the platform holder's margins. While the UK lawsuit has been dismissed, similar suits in Australia, Netherlands, Portugal, and the US could still rock the division's foundations if they make significant headway.
